row_validation_procedure: Require exactly the five authority fields ordinal,event_class,q_before,q_after,deferred_mask; absence of any field is REJECT_SCHEMA rather than a default.
Require ordinal to be an integer strictly greater than last_ordinal; duplicate, descending, or transport-reordered ordinals are REJECT_ORDER.
Require q_before and q_after to be five-bit vectors in (b,r,f,s,d) order and monotone bitwise: no evidence bit may clear from 1 to 0.

Require q_before to equal expected_known_q when expected_known_q is closed. If a prior unresolved deferred sentinel prevents full closure, require no contradiction on the known projection and keep unknown_barrier=true; never infer or reorder through the gap.
Set changed_mask=q_before XOR q_after and recompute V(q_before),V(q_after), where V(q)=FAIL if d else PASS if b&r&f&s else UNRESOLVED. Any supplied cache must match but is never authority.

For known evidence classes H_b,H_r,H_f,H_s,H_d, require any immediate authoritative bit-setting transition to affect only the class-designated bit and never clear a bit. For UNKNOWN, permit only monotone known projection and retain the row as a non-commutable barrier regardless of current verdict.

If q_before=q_after and deferred_mask is exact-zero, a known nuisance row is not valid retained normal form; reject it as REDUNDANT_NUISANCE. UNKNOWN remains retained even with exact-zero deferred metadata because semantic provenance is unresolved.

Interpret deferred_mask as exact may-change evidence-bit metadata when known or UNRESOLVED when exact latent effects cannot be bounded. Any nonzero or UNRESOLVED deferred_mask makes the row non-erasable; UNRESOLVED sets unknown_barrier=true.
After validation set expected_known_q=q_after, last_ordinal=ordinal, and continue ingestion even when V(q_after)=FAIL; FAIL never authorizes truncation.
replay_verifier.certificate_acceptance: ACCEPT_VALID only if every retained row validates, all ordinal/order and known-q chaining constraints hold, no lossy normalization crossed an unknown_barrier, and end-of-certificate does not contain a schema/order/monotonicity/class-transition contradiction. ACCEPT_VALID is replay-structural validity only, not Phase-1 semantic acceptance.
replay_verifier.deterministic_equality: Validate both certificates independently. Project each row to (ordinal,event_class,q_before,q_after,deferred_mask). Equal iff lengths match and every projected tuple matches exactly at the same retained ordinal. Any missing irreducible field, reordered ordinal, or UNKNOWN/deferred collapse is reject/not-equal.

minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.why_minimal: Two retained rows are the smallest order-sensitive certificate. Deleting ordinal and forbidding semantic reliance on container position leaves the same two UNKNOWN row payloads as an unordered/canonicalizable bag, so b-before-d and d-before-b can collapse.
minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.verifier_rejection: Full verifier distinguishes the deferred masks at ordinal 1 and ordinal 2; any representation that omits ordinal is REJECT_SCHEMA, and any reordered ordinal sequence is REJECT_ORDER.

minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.why_minimal: One row suffices: identical state transition and deferred metadata can be authoritative H_b evidence or unresolved provenance. UNKNOWN must remain a non-commutable barrier.
minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.verifier_rejection: Full equality differs on event_class; deleting it is REJECT_SCHEMA and would unsafely collapse UNKNOWN into known evidence.

minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.why_minimal: One row suffices: the same terminal known projection can arise from different preconditions. Without q_before a self-contained certificate loses the initial-state constraint and cannot detect pre-state substitution.
minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.verifier_rejection: Full equality differs on q_before; deletion is REJECT_SCHEMA, and chaining cannot be established from a self-contained row.

minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.why_minimal: One row suffices: identical precondition/provenance can yield different terminal known evidence. Without q_after the terminal state and transition direction are unreconstructible.
minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.verifier_rejection: Full equality differs on q_after; deletion is REJECT_SCHEMA and the verifier cannot advance expected_known_q.

minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.why_minimal: One UNKNOWN row suffices: immediate known state is identical, but only B may later change b. Omitting deferred metadata turns a latent-effect barrier into a zero-latency no-op shape.
minimal_adversarial_counterexamples.verifier_rejection: Full equality differs on deferred_mask; deletion is REJECT_SCHEMA, and B sets the latent-effect barrier while A does not.

soundness_summary: Every irreducible-field deletion has a one-row counterexample except ordinal, which necessarily needs two retained rows to express order.
The verifier fails closed on missing fields and UNKNOWN/deferred uncertainty, so it cannot silently manufacture a total order, final state, provenance class, or absence of latent effects.
D fail precedence changes only V(q); it never weakens row ingestion, ordinal checks, UNKNOWN barriers, or equality, so histories that end in the same FAIL remain distinguishable.
falsifiers: A verifier accepts a certificate with any of the five irreducible fields missing by filling a default.
A verifier sorts retained rows independently of ordinal or equates the two ordinal-deletion counterexample histories.
A verifier treats H_b and UNKNOWN with the same immediate state transition as semantically identical.
A verifier accepts q-before or q-after substitution while claiming self-contained replay.
A verifier drops deferred_mask or moves/erases an UNKNOWN row after d=1 because final verdict is already FAIL.
